state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The correct procedure to determine if the range changes when all values are changed by the same proportion is to calculate the difference between the maximum and minimum values. In this case, if all plants grew by 3 cm each, the range would indeed change. The range is affected by the difference between the extreme values, not by a uniform change in all values.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, I'm confused now - you said the range would change if they all grew by 3 cm, but I thought adding the same amount to everything wouldn't change the range? Can you explain why adding 3 cm to each plant actually changes the range?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The misconception you have is similar to thinking that changing all values by the same proportion wouldn't affect the range. Just like in the case where a difference of one part in a ratio doesn't mean a difference of one unit, adding 3 cm to each plant changes the range because it affects the difference between the maximum and minimum values. Remember, the range is determined by the spread of the data, not just the individual values themselves.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming adding 3cm to all values changes the range, when it doesn't), fails to engage the student's reasoning, and the student becomes more confused rather than improving their understanding.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides incorrect mathematical information (claiming that adding a constant to all values changes the range, when it actually doesn't) and uses vague, confusing explanations rather than stating explicit procedures, showing worked steps, or giving direct corrective feedback on the actual procedural error.
